BoC’s Gravelle says policy scenarios help build credibility
articles.expand: Bank of Canada Deputy Governor Toni Gravelle discussed how the central bank uses scenarios to explain how it might respond as economic conditions change. Bank of Canada scenarios are designed to help keep the BoC accountable and build credibility. When the public trusts the BoC to keep inflation around 2%, their inflation expectations stay anchored. If inflation expectations are anchored, that makes monetary policy more effective. articles.title: Australian wages jump 1.1%, strongest since 2023, but real pay falls for a fourth quarter
articles.expand: The headline beat should support the Australian dollar and short-dated yields at the margin, as traders reassess how firmly they had ruled out another RBA hike. The detail limits the hawkish case, though. Private sector strength came from a one-off award decision, public sector pay is doing much of the work, and real wages are still falling, so it’s hard to argue wages are driving inflation. That mix makes a large repricing of December less likely. For AUD/USD, rate expectations at home are still competing with a Fed on a hiking path. --- Preview here: Economic and event calendar in Asia 18 No...

articles.title: Japan’s trade deficit comes in at half the expected size as exports jump 20.5%
articles.expand: The narrower deficit is mildly supportive for the yen because it reduces the yen sold to pay for imports. Rate differentials still dominate, though, and USD/JPY remains pinned near 160 while the Fed is on a hiking path. Oil is the key swing factor: Japan’s import bill is highly sensitive to crude prices during the Iran war, so any renewed rise in oil would quickly reverse today’s improvement. For the BOJ, the data adds to evidence that the economy can absorb a December hike, which could nudge short-end JGB yields higher. Exporters with heavy chip exposure should find support in Tokyo trade. --...

articles.title: Kuroda, once Japan’s great easer, says BOJ rates may need to rise above neutral
articles.expand: For Japanese rates and the yen, a call for above-neutral rates from the architect of Japan’s easing era adds weight to the hawkish tail of BOJ pricing. Most economists see a terminal rate near 1.75%, and talk of 2.5% now has a high-profile backer. Kuroda no longer sets policy, so the direct effect is limited. Still, his critique of the food tax cut puts the fiscal-monetary tension in sharp relief ahead of an expected December hike. articles.title: RBA minutes: 6 members saw rates “not clearly sufficient”, 3 warned of sharper downturn
articles.expand: On balance the minutes lean hawkish, unsurpisngly. The majority’s view that 4.85% is “not clearly sufficient” sits awkwardly with market pricing that had all but ruled out further hikes, and it backs up Bullock’s comment this morning about upside risks. The minority’s warning of a sharper downturn sets a high bar for a December move, though. This week’s wage and jobs data, and the October CPI jump the staff flagged in advance, matter more than usual. For the Australian dollar, near 0.6730, the minutes are mildly supportive but unlikely to change the trend while policy diverges from the Fed. Th...

articles.title: RBA’s Bullock says inflation risks still skewed to upside ahead of 6-3 vote minutes
articles.expand: Bullock’s comment pushes back modestly against market pricing that has all but ruled out a December hike. It could offer the Australian dollar some support after it fell this week to its lowest level since late January. One line on a panel is unlikely to shift pricing on its own, so the minutes are the bigger test. Any sign that the majority on the board saw a real chance of further tightening would firm up the hawkish reading of Bullock’s remarks. If the minutes play up how close the vote was, front-end rates may decide the governor’s comment is a hedge, not a signal. - Minutes preview here: ...

articles.expand: Neither release is likely to move the New Zealand dollar much on its own. The Financial Stability Report assesses risk rather than signalling policy, and the food price data is only a small input into quarterly inflation. The RBNZ’s warning that recent cost pressures and higher interest rates could reverse the easing in domestic stress points in a cautious direction. Its list of global risks, from Middle East energy disruption to an AI valuation correction, reads like a list of the shocks that tend to hurt risk-sensitive currencies like the kiwi. --- Coming up later from neighbouring Australia...

articles.title: Tiff Macklem should have been fired, not celebrated
articles.expand: Tiff Macklem announced that he will retire after his seven-year term ends in June 2027. He should have left much sooner. It continues to baffle me that no central banker paid the price for the disastrous covid inflation. In no other high-profile field in the world is incompetence tolerated to the extent it is in central banking. It's a field that's protected both by government independence and a culture that accepts failure. No one exemplified that more than Tiff Macklem and his performance during the pandemic. Despite a raging housing bubble, his bank cut rates to 0.25% in the pandemic. On it...

articles.title: BOJ’s Takata calls for nimble hikes after 1.5% bid, says neutral rate may top estimates
articles.expand: Takata’s speech is the clearest public argument yet for a faster BOJ hiking pace than markets assume. He rejects a fixed quarterly rhythm and argues for reaching the middle of the neutral range early, which puts a move beyond 1.5% within view. Because his views are his own and he has been outvoted, it doesn’t change December pricing by itself. But it supports the yen and adds upward pressure on front-end JGB yields, especially with USD/JPY near 160.
